cards.text: Friend, Paul the apostle wrote this letter to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7), and he's coming down the home stretch. He's taught them a LOT, and now he tells them he's convinced they're full of goodness and brimming with knowledge. Now, when somebody tells you you're GREAT, you start bracing for the "but"... and I'm already bracing.

cards.question: Paul says the believers in Rome are full of goodness and brimming with knowledge. What else does he say they're able to do?

cards.text: And there it is, friend, there's the however! Paul says he has written to them boldly on some points.

cards.question: Paul says the believers in Rome are already brimming with knowledge. However, he calls what he's written them a bold ___ on some points.
Paul is writing boldly to believers who already know a lot. Why does he say he can?

answers.text: Because of the grace God has given him
Because the church in Rome asked him to
Because he started the church in Rome

cards.text: That grace gave Paul a job: to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles. And he describes that job like a priest's work, the priestly service of the gospel of God.

cards.question: Paul's work is priestly service. He does it so the Gentiles might become an ___ acceptable to God.
Paul says the Gentiles who become an offering to God are made holy by the Holy Spirit.

cards.text: So Paul says he exults in Christ Jesus in his service to God. Friend, the man is THRILLED about this work.

cards.question: Paul is thrilled about his work among the Gentiles. When he talks about it, what does he say he'll speak about?

answers.text: Only what Christ accomplished through him
Only what he did in his own strength
Only what the other apostles have done

cards.text: Christ led the Gentiles to obedience through Paul, by word and deed, by signs and wonders, and by the power of the Spirit of God. If all that got done through ME, I'd have it stitched on my apron in CAPITAL letters.

cards.question: Paul says he has fully proclaimed the gospel of Christ from Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum.

cards.text: Now Paul tells them what he has aspired to in all that preaching.

cards.question: What's Paul's goal for where he preaches the gospel?

answers.text: Where the churches were already strong

cards.text: Paul says he doesn't want to be building on someone else's foundation. Some folks buy the house that's already built, but Paul is out there shopping for EMPTY LOTS.

cards.question: Paul backs up his plan of preaching where Christ was not known by quoting Isaiah 52:15. It says those who were never told will never see.

cards.text: Now Paul turns to his travel plans. He says all that preaching where Christ wasn't known is why he's often been kept from coming to Rome.

cards.question: Paul says that in the regions where he has fully proclaimed the gospel, there are still plenty of opportunities left for him.

cards.text: No more opportunities there, and Paul has longed to visit them for many YEARS. That's the group chat that's been promising to get together since forever, and somebody FINALLY starts making a plan.

cards.question: Paul is finally planning his visit to the believers in Rome. He hopes to see them on his way to where?
Paul plans to pass straight through Rome on his way to Spain without stopping.

cards.text: Paul wants to enjoy their company for a while. Then they can equip him for his journey.
But not yet. First Paul is on his way to Jerusalem to serve the saints there, the classic "I'll be RIGHT there, I just gotta make one stop."
Here's what that stop is about. The believers in Macedonia and Achaia, two regions in Greece, were pleased to make a contribution.

cards.question: The believers in Macedonia and Achaia made a contribution, and Paul is taking it to Jerusalem. Who is it for?

answers.text: The poor among the saints there
The priests serving at the temple

cards.text: They were pleased to give, and Paul says these Gentile believers owe it to them too. Friend, that's the rarest thing in the world: somebody who's GLAD to pay what they owe.

cards.question: Paul says if the Gentiles have shared in the spiritual blessings of the saints in Jerusalem, they are obligated to minister to them. With what kind of blessings?
Paul plans to set off for Spain first and deliver the gift to Jerusalem afterward.

cards.text: So here's the plan: safely deliver the gift to Jerusalem, then set off for Spain by way of Rome. Friend, my biggest trip in YEARS was from the counter to the back of the junk drawer.

cards.question: Paul says he knows that when he comes to Rome, he will come in the fullness of the blessing of Christ.

cards.text: Then Paul asks them for something. He urges them, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, to join him in his struggle.

cards.question: Paul urges the believers in Rome to join him in his struggle. How?

answers.text: By praying to God for him
By sailing to Jerusalem with him

cards.question: Paul asks the believers in Rome to pray that he's delivered from the ___ in Judea, and that his service in Jerusalem is ___ to the saints there.

cards.text: All so that, by God's will, he can come to them with joy and be refreshed together with them. Then he closes this part with a blessing: "The God of peace be with all of you. Amen."
